description: Quantum backtracking, after Montanaro, decides whether a backtracking tree holds a solution with a quantum walk on the tree instead of a depth-first scan. A predicate accepts a node as a solution, rejects it, or lets it branch into children. Nodes at even depth form one set and nodes at odd depth the other; for each unsolved node the walk reflects about the star of that node and its children, with the root's children weighted by `√n` for the depth bound `n`, and a solution's reflection is the identity. One walk step reflects first the even, then the odd set. A solution gives the walk an eigenvalue-1 eigenvector with weight at least `1/2` on the root, so phase estimation from the root with `K` outcomes, `K` the next power of two of `2·√(T·n)` for `T` nodes, measures outcome `0` with probability at least `1/2`, and at most about `1/4` without one. Detection repeats the run and reports a solution when more than `3/8` of the runs see outcome `0`; finding descends from the root into the first child whose subtree detects one, checking each node on the way classically, so a returned node is always a solution. One walk step and one classical check each count as one query: a detection run costs `K − 1`, against up to `T` for classical backtracking. The simulator lists the tree once to build the walk, uncounted, and uses the exact `T` and `n`; it computes the outcome-0 probability exactly and samples the runs from it.
